title: Inference Playground — dev sandbox idea (scratch)
content:
TL;DR
Quick scratch for an "Inference Playground": an interactive, localish sandbox where engineers can replay sample traffic, tweak routing/policy knobs (batching, quant, model variant, cache toggles), and instantly see modeled cost/latency/quality tradeoffs. Aim: let product/devs evaluate serving configs fast without spinning infra or needing a full dedicated environment.

Context / problem
- Teams repeatedly ask: how will a model/quant/profile behave for our workload?
- Current workflow: run perf experiments in dev infra (slow), or provision dedicated nodes (costly), or guess using dashboards (post-hoc).
- Barriers: slow iteration, lack of realistic request mixes, no easy way to compare strategies (routing -> fallback behaviors, cache enabled/disabled), and unclear cost impact per change.

Target users
- Platform engineers wanting to validate autoscale / routing policies
- App engineers experimenting with model variants and quantization impact
- Solutions engineers making recommendations to customers

Value proposition
- Fast feedback loop: change knobs, run a synthetic replay or sample of real traces, get cost/latency/quality estimates in <1–2 minutes
- Safe: runs sandboxed, can use sampled logs or user-provided test sets, no customer data leakage (clear warnings + scrubber options)
- Shareable: snapshot configs + results can be exported and attached to PRs / issues

MVP feature set (what feels minimal yet useful)
1) Request replay engine
   - Accepts small trace uploads (ndjson of requests) or choose curated templates (chat-heavy, short prompts, long-context, embeddings-batch).
   - Simple rate/time scaling knob (x1, x10, x100) to emulate throughput effects.
2) Knob panel (per-request and global)
   - Model variant selector (gptx-13b, gptx-13b-quant, gptx-7b)
   - Batching toggle & max batch size
   - KV caching: off / prefix-cache / full-kv (simulate hit rates)
   - Quantization profile selector (none / int8 / int4)
   - Routing policy: prefer-low-latency / prefer-low-cost / region-bound
3) Cost & latency estimator
   - Lightweight estimator that maps token counts + batch sizes + model profile to expected p50/p95 latency and token cost (based on internal perf table)
   - Visualize per-request breakdown + aggregated cost per day / month with scaling assumptions
4) Quality measurement (basic)
   - Diff against a reference output for a subset (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim); allow pluggable eval scripts later
5) Snapshot + share
   - Export config + results as a small JSON bundle or permalinks in Console (if user has access)
6) Simple UI: single-page with left panel for knobs, center for replay results table, right for graphs

User stories (short)
- As an app engineer, I want to upload 1k sampled prompts and flip quantization to int8 to see delta in latency and estimated token cost so I can choose a config for staging.
- As a platform engineer, I want to run the same trace under two different routing policies and compare p95 latency and cost per 1M tokens.
- As a solutions engineer, I want to export results to attach to a customer proposal showing expected monthly cost under recommended knobs.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Upload trace (<=5k lines) and run replay with a default config within 2 minutes end-to-end (start->results)
- Estimator uses latest perf matrix and shows p50/p95 + daily/monthly cost
- UI presents side-by-side comparison of two runs
- Export bundle contains knobs, summary metrics, and a short textual digest

Success metrics (how we'll know it's useful)
- Short term: 30% reduction in time-to-first-meaningful-estimate for internal perf requests (tracked by ticket surveys)
- Engagement: 50 unique infra + app engineers using the tool monthly within first quarter after internal release
- Business lift: number of recommendations that lead to configuration changes in production (tracked via linked rollout PRs)

Implementation notes / rough tech map
- Frontend: small React SPA (can probably live in Console as an MVP iframe or internal static app)
- Backend: lightweight service that maps trace -> simulated pipeline. Two operational modes: "estimate-only" (no GPU work, uses perf model lookup) and "replay-sim" (optionally run against small ephemeral instances in a sandbox account to collect real latencies). Start with estimate-only.
- Data: use existing perf matrices (query config service) + tokenization util. Need mapping from prompt lengths to effective token usage.
- Security: scrub uploaded traces by default (PII regexes) + show explicit warning. Option to allow un-scrubbed uploads for internal-only mode.

UX sketch / interactions (notes to self)
- Quick presets: "chat app (short)" / "llm assistant (long)" / "embeddings batch"
- After run: table of top slow requests, distribution hist, cost waterfall (model compute, batch overhead, networking)
- Comparison mode: split view with run A / run B and diffs highlighted (cost delta %, p95 delta)
- Save snapshot -> autogenerated summary like "Int8 + KV full reduced cost 37% and increased p95 by 12% on long-context workload"

Open questions / risks
- How accurate will the estimator be for new models and new hardware? Need a clear accuracy indicator and notes.
- Data sensitivity: customers may try to upload real data — we must prevent accidental leaks and provide clear warnings and scrub.
- Scope creep: adding real replay against dedicated infra will balloon cost/ops. Avoid for MVP.

Next steps / TODO (short)
- [ ] Sync with infra on perf matrix API (Alex) — blocked? queue ticket INF-789
- [ ] Quick mock of UI (Priya) — due 2025-11-11
- [ ] Prototype estimator function (Samira) using current perf table by 2025-11-18
- [ ] Write short Confluence page and link to this scratch doc

Notes to self:
- Keep this intentionally rough. Prioritize rapid internal UX vs. perfect estimator. If internal folks find it useful, we can productize.
- cc @alex (need clarity on where perf matrix is authoritative)
- Example trace generator in utils/trace-gen could be reused from sampling tool in infra repo (ask infra team)

References / inspiration
- existing "cost estimator" widget in Console (we can reuse components)
- previous infra runbook for benchmarks: GH PR #2345 in infra-benchmarks (search)

-- end scratch --
